questions.question: For a continuous strictly increasing CDF, where is the median?
options: At the point where the CDF equals $1/2$
At the point where the density equals zero
Always at zero
At the maximum of the support only

questions.question: For a random variable $X$, which condition on a real number $m$ is necessary and sufficient for $m$ to be a median of $X$?
options: $\mathbb{P}(X\le m)=1/2$
$\mathbb{P}(X\le m)\ge 1/2$ and $\mathbb{P}(X\ge m)\ge 1/2$
$\mathbb{P}(X\le m)\ge 1/2$ or $\mathbb{P}(X\ge m)\ge 1/2$
$\mathbb{P}(X< m)\ge 1/2$ and $\mathbb{P}(X> m)\ge 1/2$

questions.question: $X$ takes the values $0,1,2,3$ with probabilities $1/8,3/8,3/8,1/8$. What is the set of all medians of $X$?

A random variable takes the values $1,2,100$, each with probability $1/3$. The value $100$ is replaced by $1000$; the other values and all probabilities stay the same. How do the median and the mean change?
options: The median increases, while the mean stays the same
The median stays $2$, while the mean increases by $300$
Both the median and the mean stay the same
Both the median and the mean increase by $300$

questions.question: For a random variable $X$, $\mathbb{P}(X\le 4)=0.6$ and $\mathbb{P}(X\ge 4)=0.7$. Which assessment is correct?
options: $4$ is not a median, because the two probabilities sum to more than $1$
$4$ is not a median, because $\mathbb{P}(X\le 4)$ must equal $1/2$
$4$ is not a median, because $\mathbb{P}(X>4)=0.4$ is below $1/2$
$4$ is a median, because both probabilities are at least $1/2$

questions.question: $X$ takes the value $0$ with probability $0.7$ and the value $1$ with probability $0.3$. Which statement about the medians of $X$ is correct?
options: $0$ is the unique median, although $F_X(m)=1/2$ has no solution
$X$ has no median, because $F_X(m)=1/2$ has no solution
Every $m\in[0,1]$ is a median, since $X$ has two possible values
The mean $0.3$ is the unique median

questions.question: For a CDF $F$, let $F^{-1}(u)=\inf\{x\in\mathbb{R}\colon F(x)\ge u\}$ for $0<u<1$. Which statement holds for every distribution?
options: $F^{-1}(1/2)$ is the unique median
$F^{-1}(1/2)$ is a median, but there may be other medians
$F^{-1}(1/2)$ equals the mean whenever the mean exists

questions.question: $Y$ is uniformly distributed on $[-3,3]$, so its unique median is $0$. What is the median of $Y^{2}$?
A random variable $X$ has density $f(x)=2x$ for $0\le x\le1$ and $f(x)=0$ otherwise. What is the median of $X$?
options: $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
